title: My Future Bride
amb: waves crashing on rocks at dawn with gulls, then calm cave water lapping on marble steps with dripping echoes, then quiet marble hall with soft footsteps and muffled ocean hum

lines.text: Beneath Saltpoint Coast, behind the Tidal Gate, lies a kingdom of the sea.
By its oldest law, the prince cannot be crowned until he takes a bride. The council has already chosen one for him. Prince Rian has refused her.
And when the gate glows, any human who finds it is kept... and made to forget.
Saltpoint Coast. Six twelve in the morning. Cold wind, wet rock under your boots, gulls fighting overhead.
[urgent] Look! The water's glowing! Hold on, I need this shot!
She crouches at the edge of the tide pool, camera up, her mustard hood flapping. Below the surface, blue light pulses like a heartbeat. Then the rock under her heel gives way.
A wave folds over her. The yellow jacket is gone.
You shout her name. You don't think. You dive.
The cold hits your chest hard. Salt burns your nose. The roar fills your ears. You kick toward the light until your lungs start to ache.
Something wraps around your waist. It's strong and steady. A long silver-blue tail flashes past your legs, and the sea pulls you somewhere else.
Air. You're coughing on marble steps. Water laps behind you. Drops echo from a cave ceiling.
[softly] Easy. You're breathing. Good. Keep doing that.
His voice is young, close, a little amused. When you turn, he's already stepping back to give you room. He's on two legs now, in a coat of deep-sea blue that's still dripping.
You ask him where you are.
The Tidal Gate. Right under your coast. You dove after someone, didn't you?
You grab his sleeve. My friend. Yellow jacket. Where is she?
Inside. Come on. Stay close.
He leads you up into a long marble hall. Pillars. Soft footsteps. The ocean hums through the walls. Your wet socks squeak with every step.
At the end of the hall, a woman is waiting. She has silver at her temples and a dark blue book open in her hands.
Rian. You know this wing is closed.
Her eyes move to you. Calm. Measuring.
Your friend is safe. She is resting, and she is being looked after. You, however, are not registered.
Unregistered visitors are held, and their memory of this place is sealed. That is the law. I keep it.
Sealed. Your mouth goes dry. Mila, this morning, this whole hall. All of it, gone?
You step toward her. You tell her you are not leaving without your friend.
Then you will be held until the registry decides. Guards.
Footsteps close in behind you. Metal rings on marble.
No need.
He moves to your side. Not in front of you. Beside you, his shoulder almost touching yours.
She is with me.
The whole hall seems to hold its breath.
My future bride.
You stare at him. He doesn't look back. He's smiling at the regent as if this were the easiest thing in the world.
[low] Play along. I'll take you to her.
Only you hear it. Near his ear, something glints faint blue, then fades.
A bride. The council chose your match months ago, and you refused her. Now you bring me a stranger from the tide.
Her pen hovers over the page. Then she looks straight at you.
Is that true?
The guards wait. The prince waits. Somewhere past these walls, Mila is waiting too.

prompt: The regent's pen hovers over her book, and the whole hall is waiting for your answer. Do you play along with the prince, or call him out right here?
choices: "Yes. I'm his future bride." I take his arm.
"Your bride? Since when am I your bride?"
